structured.answer: I haven't decided. I'll ask my son and someone at work. On 30,000 the employer puts in 2,250 a month against my 750, which seems worth having if I leave it six years. But the example fund is shares ("S&P500", "המדינה לא ערבה", goes up and down), not a deposit, so I'd ask for a safer track.

stuck.why: The text above says 6 years, but the chart opens at 5 years and shows a big red tax of −64,761. I didn't understand why until the brown warning box a screen later.

stuck.where: Bars at the bottom of the calculator
stuck.why: +135,000 from the employer and then −64,761 in tax. I couldn't tell whether joining is good or bad.

My salary is 30,000. I couldn't tell whether the deposit above 15,712 is still worth it or only gets taxed.

findings.what: The calculator opens at 5 years, before the tax exemption, so the first big number is a red tax of −64,761. It's frightening, and it contradicts the '6 years' in the text.
The example track is shares, 'עוקב מדד S&P500', with English letters. It isn't clear that there are safer tracks.
A dark background with grey text tires the eyes. Some lines are too small and pale.
